name: intolerance
description: Outwardly reacting negatively to something annoying or painful, when you could have could have resisted reacting.
perceptions: I could do something about it to make myself feel a little better without making the situation worse.
Of course I'll try to make it feel better.
examples: Yelling at the kids to be quiet while you're working at home.

variations.name: social intolerance
variations.description: Treating someone negatively due to a social behavior or characteristic that you don't accept.
perceptions: Someone has a behavior or characteristic that is annoying or socially wrong.
I should do or say something about it to make them and my social group know how I feel.
desires: desire to be perceived a certain way
examples: Shouting at someone who's politics you disagree with.
Treating someone negatively because they're a social outsider.

guidance.description: If you decide that you'd like be more tolerant of something, see the guidance for tolerance.

variations.name: low tolerance of discomfort
variations.description: A sense that someone else cannot experience discomfort without complaining or trying to make the situation better at the expense of others.
perceptions: That person is in a state of pain or discomfort.
They're overreacting to get attention or sympathy.
examples: Someone overreacts to a mosquito in the room.
Someone asks to turn the AC up when it's just slightly warm in the room.

guidance.description: You might consider being tolerant of their low tolerance, or you could gently suggest they consider guidance on stress sensitivity.

commentaries.quote: I have seen great intolerance shown in support of tolerance.

If we extend unlimited tolerance even to those who are intolerant, if we are not prepared to defend a tolerant society against the onslaught of the intolerant, then the tolerant will be destroyed, and tolerance with them.
Men build too many walls and not enough bridges.
